examples.en: My father tills the field with a hoe.
I went out to the garden plot carrying a hoe.

examples.ko: 괭이가 무뎌서 흙이 잘 안 파져요.
examples.en: The hoe is dull, so the soil doesn't dig well.
I washed the soil off the hoe with water.
The hoe handle broke, so I bought a new one.

examples.ko: 이 괭이는 날이 넓어서 쓰기 편해요.
examples.en: This hoe has a wide blade, so it's easy to use.

explain: 밭을 파고 일구는 농기구예요. 작은 '호미'는 쪼그려 앉아 잡초를 매는 데 쓰고, 괭이는 서서 흙을 크게 파는 데 써서 쓰임이 달라요. 도시에서는 텃밭이나 농촌 이야기에서 만나는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a farm tool used to dig and break up soil. A small '호미' is used while squatting to weed, whereas a 괭이 is used standing to dig soil in bigger strokes. In cities you mostly meet the word in talk about garden plots or the countryside.

examples.en: It's a humble place, but please sit comfortably.
The room was shabby, but it was a home with a warm heart.

examples.ko: 누추하게 사는 것 같아도 늘 깨끗하게 청소해요.
examples.en: It may look like a shabby life, but I always clean thoroughly.
It's an old inn, so it looks shabby from the outside.

examples.ko: 이사 간 집이 너무 누추해서 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: The house we moved into was so shabby that it hurt me.

examples.ko: 누추하다고 생각했는데 막상 들어가 보니 아늑했어요.
examples.en: I thought it would be shabby, but once I went in, it was cozy.

explain: 손님을 부를 때 '누추한 곳에 오셨네요'처럼 자기 집을 낮춰서 말하는 인사로도 써요. 남의 집이나 사람에게 직접 쓰면 실례가 돼요. '허름하다'가 낡은 느낌이라면 이 말은 초라하고 지저분한 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is also used as a humble greeting when you invite a guest and run down your own home, as in '누추한 곳에 오셨네요'. Using it directly about someone else's home or person is rude. While '허름하다' just feels old, this word feels more poor and dirty.

examples.en: My grandmother lives in a one-story house with a yard.
A one-story house has no stairs, so it's comfortable to live in.

examples.ko: 시골에서 작은 단층집을 한 채 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a small one-story house in the countryside.
Most houses in this neighborhood are one-story.
Since it's a one-story house, I don't worry about noise from upstairs.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 살던 단층집이 아직도 생각나요.
examples.en: I still remember the one-story house I lived in as a child.

explain: '이층집'과 대비되는 말이에요. 아파트나 빌라와 달리 한 층으로 된 개인 주택을 떠올리는 말이고, '단층 주택'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It contrasts with '이층집' (a two-story house). It brings to mind a one-floor private home, unlike an apartment or villa, and it can also be called '단층 주택'.

examples.en: I filled a basin with water and washed my hands.

examples.ko: 빨래를 큰 대야에서 발로 밟아 빨았어요.
examples.en: I washed the laundry in a big basin by stepping on it.
It's handy to have a small basin.

examples.ko: 물이 넘치지 않게 대야를 조심히 들었어요.
examples.en: I carried the basin carefully so the water wouldn't spill.

examples.ko: 비가 새서 방 안에 대야로 물을 받았어요.
examples.en: The roof leaked, so I caught the water in a basin inside the room.
This basin is plastic, so it's light.

explain: '세숫대야'처럼 앞에 용도를 붙여 말하는 일이 많아요. 부엌에서 음식을 섞을 때는 '양푼'이나 '볼'을 쓰고, 씻거나 빨래할 때는 '대야'를 써요. 요즘은 수도에서 바로 씻어서 예전만큼 자주 보이지 않아요.
explain_en: People often add the purpose in front, as in '세숫대야' (face-washing basin). In the kitchen, a mixing bowl is '양푼' or '볼', while '대야' is for washing and laundry. Because people now wash straight at the tap, you see it less than before.

examples.ko: 오래된 사진이 빛바래서 얼굴이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The old photo has faded, so I can't see the faces well.

examples.ko: 할머니 방에는 빛바랜 가족사진이 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A faded family photo hangs in my grandmother's room.
The curtains have faded in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 빛바랜 청바지를 일부러 사는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people buy faded jeans on purpose.
Even if the book cover fades, the contents stay the same.
This letter has faded, but it is precious to me.

explain: 오래돼서 색이 옅어진 사진, 종이, 옷에 써요. '빛바랜 사진'처럼 '-ㄴ' 형태로 가장 자주 들어요. 추억이나 명성이 희미해졌다는 비유로도 쓰는데, 이때는 글에서 더 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used for photos, paper and clothes whose color has become pale with age. You will most often hear the '-ㄴ' form, as in '빛바랜 사진'. It can also be used figuratively for memories or fame that have faded, mostly in writing.

examples.en: Water is leaking from the joint of the water pipe.

examples.ko: 이음매가 거의 안 보이게 벽지를 붙였어요.
examples.en: I put up the wallpaper so the seam is almost invisible.

examples.ko: 바닥 이음매 사이에 먼지가 잘 껴요.
examples.en: Dust easily gets stuck between the joints in the floor.
I filled the joint between the two boards with glue.
Please check whether the joint is sturdy.

examples.ko: 철로 이음매 부분에서 덜컹 소리가 나요.
examples.en: There's a clunking sound at the joint of the railway track.

explain: 물건과 물건이 이어지는 자리를 말해요. 옷감을 바느질해 이은 선은 보통 '솔기'라고 하고, 파이프, 벽지, 바닥처럼 이어 붙인 곳에는 '이음매'를 써요. 비유로 서로 연결되는 부분을 말할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to the spot where two things are joined. The stitched line in fabric is usually called '솔기', while '이음매' is used for pipes, wallpaper, floors and other joined parts. It can also be used figuratively for a connecting point.

examples.en: Electric current is flowing through the wire, so don't touch it.

examples.ko: 전류가 너무 세면 기계가 고장 나요.
examples.en: If the current is too strong, the machine breaks.
In the experiment, I measured the strength of the current.
It's dangerous if electric current passes through your body.
The current from the battery lights up the bulb.
To cut off the current, switch off the power first.

explain: 전류는 전기가 도선을 따라 흐르는 흐름이에요. 학교 과학이나 안전 이야기에서 '전류가 흐르다', '전류가 세다'처럼 써요. 전기를 일으키는 힘인 '전압'과, 전기 자체를 가리키는 '전기'와 구별해서 알아 두세요.
explain_en: 전류 is the flow of electricity along a wire. You see it in school science and safety talk, as in '전류가 흐르다' and '전류가 세다'. Keep it separate from '전압' (voltage) and '전기' (electricity itself).

examples.en: There are many small gears inside a watch.
I observed the gears turning as they meshed.
I oiled the bicycle's gear.

examples.ko: 톱니바퀴 하나가 고장 나면 전체가 멈춰요.
examples.en: If one gear breaks, the whole thing stops.
I'm a part of the big cogwheel called the company.
The child eagerly assembled a gear toy.

explain: 기계 부품을 말하지만 큰 조직 안에서 맡은 일만 반복하는 사람을 비유할 때도 자주 써요. 외래어 '기어'는 자동차나 자전거의 속도 조절 장치를 말할 때 더 흔해요.

phrases.example: 두 부서의 일이 톱니바퀴처럼 맞물려 돌아가요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이나 일이 빈틈없이 이어져 잘 돌아간다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes people or tasks fitting together smoothly with no gaps.

explain_en: It names a machine part, but is also used figuratively for a person who just repeats their role inside a big organization. The loanword 기어 is more common for the speed gears of cars and bikes.

examples.en: This chair has armrests, so it's comfortable.

examples.ko: 비행기 팔걸이는 옆 사람과 같이 쓰는 거예요.
examples.en: The airplane armrest is shared with the person next to you.
I watched the movie with my arm on the armrest.

examples.ko: 소파 팔걸이가 낡아서 천을 새로 씌웠어요.
examples.en: The sofa armrest was worn out, so I put new fabric on it.

examples.ko: 팔걸이를 올리면 침대처럼 누울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you lift the armrest, you can lie down like on a bed.

examples.ko: 팔걸이 없는 의자가 더 가볍고 싸요.
examples.en: Chairs without armrests are lighter and cheaper.

explain: 의자, 소파, 자동차 좌석 옆에서 팔을 올려놓는 부분이에요. 비행기나 영화관 좌석에서는 옆 사람과 같이 쓰기도 해요. 보통 '팔걸이가 있다/없다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the part beside a chair, sofa or car seat where you rest your arm. On planes or in cinemas you may share it with the person next to you. You often say '팔걸이가 있다/없다'.
